extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, educators, and authors of scientific books/reports
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and standards used by a scientific journal reviewer when assessing books, reports, and instructional materials in fields such as meteorology, zoology, medicine, geology, and engineering. Emphasises scope, accuracy, audience-appropriateness, pedagogical utility, and technical completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry scope for museums
rubrics_metrics.description: Any such inquiry should, however, approach the subject on the broadest possible lines. The resolution passed by the Museums Association asks for a 'report upon the work of the museums of the United Kingdom in relation to industries and general culture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deal with museums as such, in relation to all their multifarious aims and activities; do not confuse museums with other social activities (industrial, educational, artistic). The inquiry must seek to bring all activities into one harmonious collaboration and should treat museums broadly rather than narrowly tied to industry or scholastic education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical forecasting: finite-difference lattice and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole history of the atmosphere is to be unrolled on computing by finite differences... The points are grouped in a lattice or chess-board with each square 200 kilometres long... The standard time-interval over which uniformity of change is preserved is six hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating numerical weather-prediction methods consider the choice of grid/representative points, spatial resolution (example: 200 km slabs), vertical levels, and timestep (example: six hours). Assess whether the chosen discretisation captures the phenomena of interest and whether smaller-scale perturbations (tornadoes, local thunderstorms) will be missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality and station distribution for forecasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the appeal of the book is for a distribution of stations to be arranged so as to give the process of calculation a better chance than the existing distribution in Europe affords... observations of pressure and temperature are taken for the centres of the 'red' slabs... observations of momentum at the centres of the 'white.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether observational networks and the spatial distribution of stations provide adequate input for the numerical method. Note that wind/velocity observations may be a significant source of error; recommend improving station distribution and measurement quality to improve forecasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of mathematical rigour vs. intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The scenes are too mathematical for the ordinary meteorologist to take part in and too meteorological for the ordinary mathematician.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the level of mathematical detail matches the target audience; avoid works that are simultaneously inaccessible to both practitioners and theoreticians. A strong work should be aimed clearly (or have separate expository material) so its content is usable by its intended readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility as teaching and examination material
rubrics_metrics.description: Finally, perhaps the most important aspect ... is that a rigorous differential equation is not necessarily useless because it cannot be integrated algebraically. It opens the way to useful exercises less stupendous than calculating the weather... the book will be a rich quarry for the teacher and examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a technical work for its value in instruction: presence of worked examples, exercises, demonstration computations, and guidance for practical classroom or examination use increases pedagogical worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between original structure and incorporation of new discoveries (textbook currency)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a demand arises for a new edition ... the problem before the editor is to decide whether the new wine of recent discovery will go with safety into the old bottle. The solution depends largely upon the adaptability of the original scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For textbook revisions evaluate whether the original organisational scheme can accommodate recent discoveries and new viewpoints; editors should revise sufficiently (not just minor updates) where the subject has entered a new phase of discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and up-to-date coverage of important subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief revision is limited to three groups of Invertebrates ... while the whole of the second volume ... has undergone little change. The medical and pathogenic significance of the Protozoa ... deserve more than the passing mention given to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that important modern topics (e.g., parasitology, embryology, developmental mechanics, Drosophila genetics in the reviewer’s example) are adequately treated rather than merely mentioned. Coverage should reflect current scientific priorities and available literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and adequacy of specific organismal/taxon treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: The account of the life-history of the common Ascaris is both wrong and misleading, and the description and figure of the hook-worm are most inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate factual accuracy of life-histories, anatomical descriptions, and figures; inadequate or incorrect treatments of taxa are serious defects in biological textbooks and require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-centred exposition for popular medical books
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has not realised the abyss which separates his training and terminology from those of his audience, and has presented them with an abbreviated version of a set of lectures to professional students rather than a discourse starting from their point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For works aimed at the lay public, start from the readers' point of view, avoid specialized terminology or explain it simply, and do not present professional-student-level material as introductory popular exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and practicality of public-health advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The practical directions with which the lecture concludes are, however, admirable: do not bother about cancer being supposed to be hereditary, avoid irritations, consult a medical man at the first suspicion of anything amiss...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popular medical texts should conclude with clear, actionable, and sensible public-health guidance; such practical directions are highly valued even if earlier exposition is technical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy and completeness of scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains numerous errors ... the author, in a professedly complete list of the chemical elements the spectra of which form well-defined series, omits oxygen, sulphur, and selenium... Except from one point of view, the work is misleading and inaccurate in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical claims for factual correctness and ensure comprehensive citation of relevant work (including national contributions). Omissions of key facts or failure to acknowledge foundational contributions undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of specimen materials and explanatory apparatus (maps, tables, diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication contains specimen weather maps, and the letterpress thoroughly explains their construction and the results which the maps provide... the numerous tables, diagrams, and maps in the latter half of the book are useful for reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional works should include specimen materials (maps, sample charts), clear explanations of how they are constructed and used, and supporting tables/diagrams to aid comprehension and practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of style and bibliographic guidance for students
rubrics_metrics.description: This little volume is honourably distinguished ... by the clearness of its style and the abundant references which will prove useful in directing the student's attention to scientific contributions that he might otherwise overlook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of prose and the presence of references/bibliographies that direct further study; clear style plus references significantly enhance a student's ability to follow up topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability and tested methods for professional handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I consists of nineteen concise chapters dealing with double-entry book-keeping in its application to farm management. Part II sets forth a simple cash-book system ... the author assures us that his simplified method of keeping accounts has stood the test of actual use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical handbooks, prioritise concise, applicable instruction and methods demonstrated or tested in practice; simplicity and evidence of real-world use are positive attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of specialist vs. general audience in technical treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment is, naturally, wholly technical, and very brief. To the expert the treatment will doubtless appeal, but to the ordinary scientific reader such sentences ... indicate a language even more formidable than his own: 'A glossary might have been added for the uninitiated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be explicit about intended readership. If a text is highly technical, consider adding glossaries or explanatory material to make portions accessible to a broader scientific audience; otherwise restrict scope to specialists.
